purpose: Assesses whether the organization can detect an adversary mapping out the internal environment after gaining access.
summary: Discovery consists of techniques adversaries use to gain knowledge about the system and internal network, such as enumerating accounts, network shares, running processes, and system configuration to plan subsequent movement and objectives.
expectedStatementElements: How the organization detects unusual enumeration activity (account, network share, process listing) on endpoints
What network monitoring identifies internal reconnaissance-style traffic (port scanning, share enumeration) distinct from normal use
How honeypots, decoy accounts, or canary tokens are used to catch discovery activity
How discovery-stage detections are correlated with earlier tactics to identify an attack in progress before lateral movement
evidenceExamples: EDR/SIEM detection rules for enumeration commands and discovery-related process activity
Internal network monitoring configuration flagging scanning or share enumeration behavior
Honeypot, decoy account, or canary token deployment documentation
Correlation rules linking discovery-stage alerts with earlier-stage indicators
commonGaps: Enumeration commands and discovery activity blend in with normal administrative behavior and go undetected
Internal network traffic isn't monitored closely enough to catch scanning or share enumeration
No honeypots, decoy accounts, or canary tokens exist to catch an adversary mapping the environment
Discovery-stage alerts aren't correlated with other tactics, so isolated signals don't trigger investigation
interviewQuestions: Would unusual account or network enumeration on an endpoint actually stand out from normal admin activity?
Is internal network traffic monitored closely enough to catch someone scanning or mapping shares?
Do you use any honeypots, decoy accounts, or canary tokens to catch this kind of activity?
If discovery activity were detected, would it get correlated with other signals, or treated as an isolated alert?
